A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DARC study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–I are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, multi-annotator human results, proxy-validation analyses, ablations, and latency measurements in Section 5 and Appendix H.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds bucketed human outcomes and perturbation-family experiments in Table 3 and Appendix H.13.

M1.justification: V1 uses style-preserving perturbations for proxy disagreement. V2 adds targeted rewrites that normalize verbosity, formatting, and sycophantic/apologetic phrasing, plus a hybrid proxy combining both families. These change the proxy inputs used by DARC-epsilon; the core entropic decoding and risk-control rules remain unchanged.

E1.justification: MT-Bench and AlpacaEval 2.0 remain the named benchmarks. V2 additionally reports an artifact-focused stress-test slice in Tables 16–17, but does not specify its source, membership, or construction. It is unclear whether this introduces distinct data/scenario coverage or analyzes a subset of previously covered data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the corresponding main and appendix experiments, including BoP(HedgeTune), Caution, DeAL, MC-Dropout, RBoN, cDPO/rDPO, and the existing CVaR/LCB comparisons. Updating Caution's citation does not introduce a new baseline; the added perturbation variants are method ablations.

E3.justification: Appendix H.13 adds a controlled comparison of style-only, targeted-only, and hybrid perturbations using the same total augmentation budget, fixed candidate pools, and held-out evaluation protocol. The hybrid allocates four rewrites to each family. Previously reported main-experiment settings and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: New Table 3 examines low- versus high-disagreement behavior through human-score differences and win/tie/loss outcomes. New Tables 16–17 test how perturbation-family choice affects proxy–human alignment and downstream robustness. Existing hyperparameter sensitivities, mismatch cases, and other supplementary analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing confidence intervals, significance reporting, seed disclosures, five-rater protocol, and bootstrap descriptions are retained. The added tables do not introduce new repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Existing headline and appendix results remain unchanged. New Table 3 reports DARC-epsilon human-score gains from 0.125 in Q1 to 1.037 in Q5. Within the new Table 17 ablation, hybrid versus style-only perturbations yield stress CVaR of 7.35 versus 6.87, alongside lower overall mean satisfaction, 7.96 versus 8.08.

T1.justification: The LCB, KL/chi-squared DRO, proxy-error, and Pareto results and their proofs are retained. The new theory–proxy paragraph restates qualifications already in Appendix A.12. The hybrid formula applies the existing standard-deviation calculation to mixed perturbations; the completed LCB pseudocode implements an already stated rule.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about retraining-free risk-sensitive decoding, its LCB/DRO interpretation, and improved disagreement/tail outcomes with competitive average quality.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly treats Tradeoff as a supporting diagnostic because it partly matches the selection objective, emphasizing held-out human satisfaction and CVaR as external validation. It also explains preserved surface cues as a limitation of style-only perturbations and interprets low-disagreement ties as limited intervention where disagreement is weak.

D1.justification: V2 supplies the targeted rewrite instruction, the hybrid allocation and aggregation procedure, and an explicit LCB branch with its parameters in Algorithm 1. The LCB addition completes documentation of an existing option. Existing hardware, training configurations, and default main-experiment settings are retained.

R1.justification: The research positioning and cited-work coverage are unchanged. Caution's anonymous submission becomes the named Yu et al. publication; the entropy-guided multi-head reward reference receives its ENCORE publication details. Other edits update bibliographic metadata rather than add distinct prior work.

P1.justification: V2 adds localized explanatory paragraphs about the theory–proxy interface, metric interpretation, and perturbation families, and expands Appendix H.13. It also corrects author/affiliation information and bibliography entries. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 3, 16, and 17 and reformats Algorithm 1, including removing line numbering. Existing plots retain their content but several figures and tables move and are renumbered. The overall visual presentation remains similar.

improvement.justification: The bucketed human outcomes and perturbation ablations modestly strengthen the empirical analysis, including exposing a robustness–mean-quality tradeoff. Completing the LCB pseudocode and qualifying the Tradeoff metric improve clarity and reproducibility. The undefined stress-test slice limits the new evidence's interpretability, so these are incremental gains rather than a substantial strengthening of the unchanged core results.
